species.name: Cahowl

dex.text: Spent three hundred years being dead and took the news badly. It now sulks in a burrow on a rock off Bermuda and only comes out after dark, to make a noise like a ghost with a head cold.
dex.fact: The cahow, Bermuda's petrel, was thought extinct for about 300 years until a nest was found in 1951; it nests in burrows on islets such as Nonsuch.

species.real: The first settlers in 1600s Bermuda ate cahows by the thousand. Before that, the birds' eerie night calls helped Spanish sailors decide the place was an island of devils.

species.name: Cahowler

dex.text: Came back from the dead once, and has since taken to wailing about it at night over the Bermuda burrows. Wins the argument every time.
dex.fact: Cahows were thought extinct for about 300 years until 1951, and conservationists now dig artificial burrows with baffles that keep bigger seabirds out.

species.real: A cahow pair raises just one chick a year, laying a single egg in the burrow in January, in the depths of Bermuda's winter.
